# Figure 2 — Two learned oscillators, in orthogonal subspaces of one table

**Generated by** `scripts/splicebert/make_fig2_oscillators.py` from
`results/phase-lattice/fig_report_data.json`. Table: **SpliceBERT.1024nt**, 1026 × 512.

## A — Both carriers are narrowband spikes

Normalised Fourier power of the position table, every bin. Most of the table's energy is **slow
positional drift** (period > 22 nt, grey) — the boring, expected part. Against that background,
exactly two narrowband components stand out: **period 3** at 289× the median bin, and **≈10.63**
at 546×. Nothing else in the spectrum is close.

## B — This is why we say "carrier," not "phase"

Bin *k* of the table is not a number. It is a complex **vector** in ℂ⁵¹², one phase per embedding
dimension. Its contribution at position *p* traces an **ellipse** in the plane spanned by
Re F[k] and Im F[k]. Circularity = σ₂/σ₁ of that plane:

- **1.0 → a circle.** Every phase in [0, 2π) is realised in *some* embedding direction, so the
  bin **has no phase of its own**.
- **0.0 → a line.** A standing wave: one phase, shared by every dimension.

Both carriers are near-perfect circles: **0.977** and **0.992**. The table therefore does not
*assign* a phase — it supplies a **rotating two-dimensional coordinate system**, and each head
**chooses** its phase from that system via its QK bilinear form. Figure 3A shows six heads doing
exactly that, landing on their chosen carrier-phase class to within 0.76°.

The period-3 carrier visits **exactly three points**. This is not a plotting choice: 1026/342 = 3
*exactly*, so position *p* can only take three angles, corresponding to position modulo 3. This
geometric fact does not identify codon phase or reading frame. The ≈10.63 carrier has no such
constraint — 1026/96 = 10.6875 is not an integer, so it
sweeps the entire circle.

## C — The two planes are disjoint

Mean squared cosine of the principal angles between the subspaces of each Fourier bin. The block
structure is the whole point: a bin overlaps its own sidebands at ≈0.9–0.99 (that is what "the
same carrier, phase-modulated" looks like), and overlaps the *other* carrier at **0.0003**. Two
independent positional channels, encoded in disjoint subspaces of the same table.

## D — "10.67" was a grid label, not a measurement

A Fourier bin is a *bin*: on a 512-row grid, bin 48 is labelled 512/48 = 10.667, and on a
1026-row grid, bin 96 is labelled 10.6875. Those labels are artefacts of the grid, and they
disagree. The **sub-bin** wavelength — recovered by inverting the sinc² leakage into
neighbouring bins — is **10.607** on one grid and **10.652** on the other, converging on
**10.630**. The grids disagree; the measurement does not.

This matters because the nucleosomal signal measured in DNA sits at **10.298** (C14), and
the difference between 10.63 and 10.30 is far larger than the fit uncertainty. Quoting the bin
label would have made the two look like the same number. They are not.
